actions.action: Rub a few specks with a cotton swab to tell mealybugs from shed skins
Shake the plant to check for flying whiteflies
Rinse the plant hard in the shower, especially leaf undersides
Swab every speck with 70% alcohol, peeling back or removing stem sheaths
Unpot and check roots and pot wall for root mealybugs
If root mealybugs found, wash roots, repot in fresh soil and scrub the pot
Apply insecticidal soap or neem every 5-7 days for 6 weeks
Add systemic imidacloprid granules to the soil where legal
Treat the whole plant collection the same way

reason: The answer correctly identifies a foliage pest infestation (mealybugs, a similar sap-sucking bug, with whiteflies as an alternative), and its first fix step, wiping with alcohol and cutting off bad leaves, matches the fix that worked; nothing it recommends is likely to harm the plant.
